newsitem.title: CANADA: Suncor plans big jump in capital spending.
newsitem.headline: Suncor plans big jump in capital spending.

text.p: Suncor Inc said on Wednesday it planned to increase its capital spending by 40 percent in 1997 to C$700 million.
Suncor said the jump was part of its aggressive growth plans that involved expanding existing businesses and branching out into new ventures.
About C$440 million was earmarked for the company's oil sands operation in Fort McMurray, Alberta.
A further $170 million would be spent on exploration and production of conventional oil and gas and C$50 million would be invested in Sunoco, Suncor's downstream division.

It said money spent in oil sands would be dedicated to expanding the company's northern Alberta plant to 105,000 barrels per day in a project now slated to be complete by January 1, 1999, about two years ahead of the previous schedule.
In exploration and production, Suncor plans to drill another two heavy oil wells at Burnt Lake and define the extent and quality of reserves at Firebag and Cheecham in northeastern Alberta.
Money spent at Sunoco will be directed to improving environmental, energy and operating efficiency as well as growing refining and retail operations, Suncor said.
Spending on ethanol blending is also slated to begin in 1997, it said. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
